title: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor
description: A trojanized build of vsftpd 2.3.4 distributed between June and July 2011 contains a backdoor that opens a root shell on TCP/6200 when a username ending in ':)' is supplied.

title: ProFTPD ftp_getline() stack buffer overflow
description: A stack-based buffer overflow in ProFTPD's response pooling allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code via a crafted response.

title: OpenSSH user enumeration via authentication timing
description: OpenSSH before 7.3 allows remote attackers to enumerate valid usernames via a timing side-channel in the auth-keyed password check for non-existent users.

title: OpenSSH username enumeration in auth-gss2 / sshd
description: OpenSSH through 7.7 is prone to a user enumeration vulnerability due to not delaying bailout for an invalid authenticating user until after the packet containing the request has been fully parsed.

title: Apache HTTP Server path traversal / RCE
description: A path traversal flaw in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49 allows mapping URLs to files outside the document root, and to source/RCE if CGI scripts are enabled.

title: SambaCry remote code execution
description: Samba versions from 3.5.0 onward are vulnerable to remote code execution via a writable share, allowing a malicious shared library to be loaded and executed by the server.

title: EternalBlue SMBv1 remote code execution (MS17-010)
description: Unpatched SMBv1 implementations are vulnerable to EternalBlue, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Version could not be determined from the scan; confirm the SMB dialect and patch level manually.

title: MySQL/MariaDB authentication bypass
description: A flaw in MySQL/MariaDB's password comparison allows an attacker to bypass authentication by repeatedly attempting to connect with any password, due to a memcmp() return value being misinterpreted on some platforms.

title: Cleartext remote administration protocol (Telnet)
description: Telnet transmits credentials and session data in cleartext, allowing trivial interception by anyone on the network path. Should be disabled in favor of SSH.

title: Cleartext file transfer protocol (FTP)
description: Standard FTP transmits credentials and file contents in cleartext. Should be replaced with SFTP/FTPS unless anonymous read-only access is intentional.

title: Cleartext / trust-based remote shell (r-services)
description: BSD r-services (rsh/rexec/rlogin) rely on IP-based trust and transmit data in cleartext, making them trivially spoofable and interceptable. Should be disabled in favor of SSH.
